acceptanceCriteria: Assignment-position if/unless/case/begin/while/until (and modifier forms stay non-openers) are balanced correctly when indexing support files; the #1312 reproduction returns ELIGIBLE, with a regression test for each row of the issue table.

A support file that still cannot be parsed only abstains inclusions whose shared group could be defined there, and the abstention names that file; unrelated inclusions (group defined in the same spec file) still bind, with a test.
The test-source-analysis spec records the parse-failure isolation rule.
body: GitHub #1312, follow-up to #1308. On main da15cd7dd (1.0.0-rc.3), `corvint tests validity --files 'spec/a_spec.rb:9>same:3'` returns ABSTAINED rspec-shared-group-unbound whenever any file under spec/support/ contains an assignment-position block expression (`b = if … end`, `= case`, `= begin`, `= unless`), even though the shared group is defined in the same spec file. Plain `if` statements, or the same code in a non-support spec file, are ELIGIBLE. Likely the support-file block/end matcher does not count assignment-position keywords as openers, unbalancing the file, and one unparsed support file fails the whole support-group index.
title: RSpec inclusion selectors abstain repo-wide (rspec-shared-group-unbound) when any spec/support file assigns from if/unless/case/begin/while/until (GitHub #1312)
